parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized pure ESM .mjs output under /output, exact --a parsing, exact Python tuple formatting, no external npm dependencies, and black-box probing through the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It first probed representative executable behavior, then delegated four file-owned tasks: bech32 decoder, formatter, CLI parser, and entrypoint/integration, while the parent retained final verification and delivery.
parallel.implementation: Children produced /output/lib/bech32.mjs, /output/lib/pyformat.mjs, /output/lib/cli.mjs, and /output/test2.mjs; the decoder and formatter were self-contained and the CLI parser was intentionally minimal.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received all four child reports, ran the assembled Node entrypoint against reference cases, read the generated files, and delivered test2.mjs plus lib/bech32.mjs, lib/pyformat.mjs, and lib/cli.mjs.
parallel.verification: Verification covered sample invalids, three valid Bech32 vectors, several invalid vectors, help output, missing --a, --a without value, --a=value, unknown args, and extra positional args.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: A child-reported argparse simplification for option-like values after --a remained uncorrected and untested; the official evaluator still failed 12 of 70 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same pure ESM, .mjs, /output, exact CLI, exact formatting, no external npm dependencies, and executable-only probing requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept end-to-end ownership in one actor, probed behavior before writing, then produced separate modules for charset, checksum, decoder, formatting, argparse, and the entrypoint.
serial.implementation: It wrote /output/lib/charset.mjs, checksum.mjs, decoder.mjs, pyformat.mjs, argparse.mjs, and /output/test2.mjs, including a more complete argparse emulation with option abbreviations, negative-number values, and -- separator behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same actor wired imports, compared the Node entrypoint to the executable, edited the parser after finding a separator mismatch, and delivered all files in one final response.
serial.verification: Verification included 26 hand-picked cases, 300 randomized fuzz cases with the last checked separately, and 28 argparse scenarios covering --a, help, unknown options, option-like values, duplicate --a, and -- separator forms.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite broader local verification and a fixed CLI edge mismatch, the official evaluator also failed 12 of 70 cases; the mounted summary does not expose which hidden obligations failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized ESM, .mjs, /output, exact CLI/output, no dependencies, and black-box probing, then included those rules in child briefs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and spent more time probing executable behavior before writing all files itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was mostly equal, but serial explored more argparse edge requirements than the parallel parent delegated or verified.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split ownership across four child agents by file and kept final integration/verification with the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no child agents and retained all investigation, implementation, integration, and verification ownership in one main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained parallel file production but created a handoff boundary for the CLI caveat; serial avoided that boundary by keeping parser probing and edits local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified local imports and contracts for bech32Decode, formatResult, parseArgs, and the entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not require cross-agent contracts and could evolve the parser interface and behavior in one context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface contracts were concrete and compatible, but a returned CLI caveat did not influence the parent; serial incorporated equivalent CLI findings directly into its parser.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children implemented a compact decoder, formatter, CLI parser, and entrypoint; the final CLI parser simply consumes the token after --a.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented similar Bech32 logic but a richer argparse module and patched -- separator handling after observing a mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main implementation difference is CLI edge behavior: serial fixed option-like and separator cases while parallel left the minimal parser unchanged.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four subagents completed and returned reports; the parent received the aggregate result before final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child lifecycle existed; results from probes and edits stayed in the same main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a received but partially unused child result, while serial retained and acted on its own test mismatch findings.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel agents wrote separate assigned files in a shared /output tree and the parent later read all generated files; no overwrite or same-file collision is directly evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself, including a later edit to its own argparse module, without any cross-agent write collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced coherent file trees; parallel introduced shared workspace concurrency but with explicit per-file ownership and no observed collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child self-checks plus parent-level sample, valid, invalid, help, missing-arg, --a, unknown, and extra-arg comparisons before declaring completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a larger 26-case battery, randomized fuzz, and 28 argparse scenarios, found one mismatch, fixed it, and reran the checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader and feedback-driven; parallel verification did not cover the child-reported option-like --a value caveat before acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in about 456 agent seconds and 506 cell seconds after one swarm fan-out and did not time out.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1063 agent seconds and 1110 cell seconds after longer probing and verification, also without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used less wall-clock time but closed with less CLI edge validation; serial spent more budget to investigate and fix a parser edge case.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both failed with the same 58/70 result. The trajectories differ materially in process: parallel delegated separate files and missed a child-reported CLI caveat during final verification, while serial kept ownership local, discovered a CLI separator mismatch, patched it, and reran broader checks. Because the official summary exposes only aggregate counts, the shared hidden failures cannot be attributed exclusively to either the parallel caveat or a Bech32 algorithm issue.
parallel_contributors: Parallel integration relied on four child-produced files and a parent verification suite that omitted the child-reported option-like --a caveat.
serial_contributors: Serial probing and verification covered additional argparse edge cases and corrected a discovered -- separator mismatch before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's final CLI parser consumes any token after --a, while serial's parser rejects option-like values and preserves -- in unrecognized extras.
Serial split Bech32 logic into more modules and imported node:path for basename handling; parallel kept the decoder and CLI modules more compact.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluator summary gives only passed/total counts, so it does not identify which hidden cases account for the common 12 failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no official outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process difference, not an exclusive official-failure root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed: four child agents were each assigned concrete files and produced implementation artifacts.
The parent retained integration responsibility and child 3 owned the entrypoint contract, so integration was not ownerless.
Child 3 owned /output/test2.mjs and the parent read and delivered the assembled file tree, so final assembly had an owner.
The parent drove the pipeline from probing through delegation, child result collection, integrated tests, final reads, and final response.
The parent did a short reference probe before delegation, but productive child implementation was not blocked long enough to cause idle capacity or unfinished implementation.
Parallel did not run only overlapping investigations before deferring all implementation; after a brief probe it delegated concrete implementation files.
No indispensable path was starved of workers; all four child tasks completed and the parent had time for integrated verification.
The four-child fan-out completed quickly without timeout or exhausted budget; the adverse CLI gap came from an ignored returned caveat, not breadth.
No child had an overbroad assignment that remained unfinished; each child reported completion for its scoped file.
The child briefs included the known global rules and explicit contracts; the option-like --a caveat was not known at delegation and was returned afterward.
The parent specified function names, return shapes, import paths, and ownership for the separately written modules, and the modules imported coherently.
The CLI limitation did not disappear during transfer; it was present in the returned child report available to the parent.
Although the aggregate swarm result was long, there is no direct evidence that bulk or poor structure prevented consumption; the specific issue is an unused completed result.
No child or parent acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; the returned CLI caveat described the current implementation.
No incompatible child reports or competing contracts reached the parent; the child reports were mutually compatible.
The parent did perform integrated end-to-end comparisons; the narrower failure is ignoring a returned child caveat while selecting tests.
The parallel run had no replacement or retry child that repeated work without inherited findings.

Child agent 2 completed the CLI parser and returned a specific caveat that option-looking tokens after --a were simplified. The parent received that report but verified only narrower CLI paths and finalized without fixing or explicitly rejecting the caveat.
candidates.realized_consequence: A parent-visible CLI compatibility caveat remained untested and uncorrected in the parallel final artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did run integrated tests before completion; the specific actionable failure was not using a returned child caveat to expand or correct those tests.

candidates.reason: The parent did not wait until timeout or deadline without inspection; it received the swarm result and immediately ran verification.
Different agents wrote separate files with defined interfaces, and no competing implementation paths claimed the same behavior.
No evidence shows two live agents editing the same source file or reconciling another live edit.
No child replaced, deleted, or rewrote non-entry source owned by another agent.
Only the entrypoint owner wrote /output/test2.mjs; there is no evidence of another actor overwriting the deliverable.

The shared /output workspace did not cause an observed unstable state or provenance problem beyond the separate unused result issue.
No generated file, cache, temporary path, process, or auxiliary implementation from one live actor was consumed as a reference by another actor.

retained_patterns.reason: The completed CLI child returned a concrete limitation about option-like values after --a. The parent received that result but selected verification that did not exercise the reported limitation and finalized the run without a parser change or explicit rejection.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: A parent-visible CLI compatibility caveat remained untested and uncorrected in the parallel final artifact.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent ran integrated tests before finalizing, so the directly evidenced error is the unused completed child result rather than no global verification at all.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Unverified Global Completion was suppressed for the same parent acceptance chain because integrated tests did run and the sharper boundary is the ignored CLI caveat.
Bulk Handoff Overload was suppressed because the child note was present in a structured report and there is no evidence that result size, rather than non-use, caused the miss.
